name: Vasopressin
executiveSummary: Antidiuretic hormone at vasopressor doses. Adult septic shock: **0.03 units/min** fixed (range **0.01–0.04 units/min**) as adjunct to norepinephrine. Pediatrics: **0.0005–0.002 units/kg/min** (**0.03–0.12 units/kg/h**). No rapid bolus unless protocol.
indications:
## Indications

- Refractory vasodilated shock / adjunct in sepsis (Surviving Sepsis).
- Central diabetes insipidus and variceal GI bleeding: **different regimens and higher doses** — do not confuse with shock dosing.

## Precautions

- Digital, mesenteric, coronary ischemia; relative hyponatremia; ↓ cardiac output if excessive afterload.
- Central line preferred. Does not replace volume or antibiotics.
- Common ampules: **20 units/mL**.

> In shock, use “low fixed” doses; exceeding 0.04 units/min usually adds little benefit and increases ischemia.

adulto.dose: Septic shock: **0.03 units/min** continuous IV (alternative titration **0.01–0.04 units/min**). Varices (other regimen): often **0.2–0.4 units/min** — hepatology/GI protocol only.
adulto.administration: Dilute in NS/D5W (common max conc. **1 unit/mL**); continuous pump.
adulto.notes: Monitor BP, lactate, peripheral perfusion, and urine output.

pediatrico.dose: Refractory shock: **0.0005–0.002 units/kg/min** (approx. **0.03–0.12 units/kg/h**); some protocols use up to **0.15 units/kg/h** — infectious diseases/ICU.
pediatrico.notes: Once diluted: discard ~18 h at room temperature / ~24 h refrigerated (local guide).

neonatal.dose: Refractory shock: **0.0003–0.002 units/kg/min** continuous IV (approx. **0.02–0.12 units/kg/h**); titrate with monitoring — neonatology.
neonatal.administration: Central IV + pump; dilute NS/D5W (max ~1 unit/mL).

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution: follow package insert/local guide (~18–24 h).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Peripheral/mesenteric ischemia, hypertension, bradycardia, arrhythmias, hyponatremia, skin necrosis if extravasation.
